baseline_measured_later.how: baseline-manual.sh: base commit, Homebrew Ruby 4.0.0 on PATH (the Ruby bin/harness picks), Gemfile.lock, config/database.yml and the SQLite test databases copied from the setup gate. The system Ruby 2.6 cannot run it: the run measured nothing.

blocked.reason: On a new SQLite3 database, bin/rails db:prepare fails every time at db/migrate/072_add_enumerations_position.rb (no such column: enumerations.position). The migration skips add_column when Enumeration.column_names already lists the column. bin/harness setup uses db:create db:migrate instead, which passes every time. The migration was not changed: a human should decide whether to fix it upstream.

uw-harness flags db/migrate/001_setup.rb as a secret-looking value. It is the SHA1 hash of the default admin password 'admin', which doc/INSTALL documents and which Redmine forces users to change at first login. It is not a real secret, and the migration may not be changed, so this check stays partial.

Left out of bin/harness check: system tests (bin/harness test-system, need Chrome and a Mermaid.js download), the Bazaar non-ASCII test (needs the en_US.ISO8859-1 locale), bundle audit (needs network), and the PostgreSQL/MySQL and Ruby 3.3/3.4 matrix. The upstream workflows tests.yml and linters.yml still run all of them.

The uw-harness package is not published on npm (npx -y uw-harness returned 404 here), so the new harness.yml workflow will fail until it is published. The gates were checked with the local build of uw-harness (check passes) and run directly from a clean shell.
Without human answers, docs/deploy.md and docs/observability.md keep open TODO blocks, so these two checks stay partial.

open_questions.question: Is this copy of Redmine deployed anywhere by your team (which server, which environments), or is it only a mirror of upstream used for development?
If this copy is deployed: who can deploy, how is a release built for it (git tag, archive, branch), and how do you roll back a release that ran database migrations?
Where do production logs go (log/production.log, STDOUT to a collector?), and is there any error tracker, dashboard or alert channel for this instance?

Should changes from agents follow the upstream process (a patch attached to an issue on www.redmine.org, commit message ending with (#issue)) or a local branch and pull request process in this repository?

May the new workflow .github/workflows/harness.yml run on pull requests in this repository, given that upstream development happens in Subversion on www.redmine.org and GitHub pull requests are not reviewed there?
Is it acceptable that the fast gate skips the SCM, LDAP and system (Chrome) tests that need external binaries or services?
Which database should be the default for local development and the gates: SQLite3 (the current default of bin/harness setup) or PostgreSQL/MySQL in Docker?

task.title: Add a test for the /up health check route
task.description: config/routes.rb exposes GET /up (rails/health#show) for load balancers and uptime monitors, but no test in test/ covers it. Add a routing test and an integration test, so that a change to the routes or to authentication filters cannot break the health check without a failing test.
acceptance: A new routing assertion (for example in test/integration/routing/) checks that GET /up routes to rails/health#show.
A new integration test checks that an anonymous GET /up returns 200, also when the setting 'login_required' is enabled.
Only files under test/ change, `bin/harness check-fast` and `bin/harness check` pass, and a dated entry is added to docs/harness/log.md.

harness_gaps.problem: AGENTS.md and the implement-change skill say to run one test with `bin/rails test <file>`. On macOS this uses the first Ruby on PATH, which is the system Ruby 2.6, and it fails with a missing-bundler error. Only bin/harness picks a supported Ruby. The docs should say to put /opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin on PATH first (or use .tool-versions with a version manager), or bin/harness should offer a task that runs a single test.

The task's criterion 'only files under test/ change' conflicts with the rule in AGENTS.md to add a docs/harness/log.md entry for each change. Nothing tells the agent which rule wins. I followed both and treated the log file as the allowed exception.

Nothing in the harness docs lists the test base classes (Redmine::RoutingTest, Redmine::IntegrationTest) or the with_settings helper. I had to read test_helper.rb and existing tests to find them. A short section in docs/local-dev.md or the implement-change skill would help.
